en: to approve; to pass (a bill or motion)

examples.en: The council passed next year's budget proposal.

examples.ko: 위원회가 법안을 가결하기까지 두 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took two hours for the committee to pass the bill.
If the votes in favor outnumber those against, the agenda item is passed.

examples.ko: 이사회는 투자 계획을 가결하지 않고 다음 회의로 미뤘어요.
examples.en: The board didn't approve the investment plan and put it off to the next meeting.

examples.ko: 시의회가 조례안을 가결한 뒤에 시행이 결정됐어요.
examples.en: After the city council passed the ordinance, its implementation was decided.

examples.ko: 의원들이 표결 끝에 개정안을 가결했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the lawmakers passed the amendment after a vote.

explain: 회의에서 표결로 안건이나 법안을 통과시킨다는 점에서 일반적인 '통과시키다'와 달라요. 반대말은 '부결하다'예요. 뉴스에서는 '가결됐다'처럼 피동 표현도 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: That bill was passed in the National Assembly yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피동 표현으로, 안건이 표결을 거쳐 통과된 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, stating the result of a motion being approved by a vote.

phrases.en: The committee members approved the item unanimously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모든 사람이 찬성해서 통과시켰다는 점을 덧붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds that everyone voted in favor when the motion was approved.

phrases.example: 가결 여부는 내일 알 수 있어요.
phrases.en: We'll know tomorrow whether it passes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안건이 통과될지 아닐지를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for whether a motion passes or not.

explain_en: Unlike the general '통과시키다', it is specifically about passing a proposal or bill by a vote at a meeting. The opposite is '부결하다' (to reject). In the news you also often see the passive form, as in '가결됐다'.

examples.en: The government announced a pension reform plan yesterday.
The debate in the National Assembly dragged on because of the reform plan.

examples.ko: 학교 교칙 개혁안에 학생들도 의견을 냈어요.
examples.en: Students also gave their opinions on the school rule reform plan.

examples.ko: 이 개혁안은 많은 사람의 반대에 부딪혔어요.
examples.en: This reform plan ran into opposition from many people.
I wonder whether the new reform plan will pass.

examples.ko: 개혁안대로 하면 월급이 줄어든다고 해서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I hear salaries will shrink if they follow the reform plan, so I'm worried.

explain: 정치나 제도 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. '계획'보다 공식적으로 제안된 방안이라는 느낌이 강해요. '개혁안을 마련하다', '개혁안을 발표하다', '개혁안이 통과되다'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The president announced an education reform plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정부나 단체가 계획을 공식적으로 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a government or group officially announces a plan.

phrases.en: The government is preparing a new reform plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발표하기 전에 방안을 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means drawing up a plan before announcing it.
phrases.en_equiv: to draw up a reform plan

phrases.en: The reform bill passed in the National Assembly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투표나 회의에서 승인받았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the plan has been approved by a vote or meeting.

explain_en: It often appears in political and policy news. It feels more like an officially proposed plan than the general word '계획'. Common patterns are '개혁안을 마련하다', '개혁안을 발표하다' and '개혁안이 통과되다'.

examples.en: Yesterday the National Assembly passed that resolution.
A new resolution was adopted at the UN Security Council.
The opposition party voiced opposition to the resolution.
The lawmakers debated the draft of the resolution.
The resolution passed with two hundred votes in favor.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리도 환경 보호 결의안을 만들어 봤어요.
examples.en: Our club also drew up an environmental protection resolution.

explain: 뉴스에서 국회, 지방 의회, 유엔처럼 회의에서 하나의 의견이나 입장을 공식으로 정하자고 내놓는 안을 말할 때 써요. '법안'은 법을 만들자는 안이고 '결의안'은 의견이나 입장을 정하자는 안이에요. '결의안이 통과되다', '채택되다', '부결되다'처럼 함께 써요.

phrases.en: The lawmakers submitted a new resolution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결의안을 회의에 올릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for putting a resolution before a meeting.

phrases.en: Most countries voted in favor of that resolution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결의안에 동의하는 입장을 밝힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when stating support for a resolution.

phrases.en: Some lawmakers opposed that resolution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결의안에 동의하지 않는다는 입장을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when stating opposition to a resolution.

explain_en: In the news it is used for a proposal put to a body such as the National Assembly, a local council or the UN to formally decide on an opinion or position. A '법안' is a proposal to make a law, while a '결의안' is one to settle an opinion or stance. It is used with verbs such as '통과되다', '채택되다' and '부결되다'.

examples.en: An international conference will be held in Seoul next month.
I took a plane to attend an international conference.
Interpreters are essential at international conferences.
I'm very busy these days preparing for the international conference.

examples.ko: 회사는 올해 국제회의를 두 번 주최했어요.
examples.en: The company hosted an international conference twice this year.
I translated the materials for the international conference into English.

explain: '국제회의가 열리다', '국제회의를 개최하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스나 업무에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: An international conference is held in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의가 어디서 언제 하는지 말할 때 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for saying where and when a conference takes place.

phrases.en: Our country is hosting an international conference this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의를 여는 쪽이 주어일 때 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the host is the subject. Common in the news.

phrases.en: My father went on a business trip to attend an international conference.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의에 가는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 업무 이야기에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the person who goes to the meeting. Fits work-related talk.

explain_en: It is used as '국제회의가 열리다' or '국제회의를 개최하다'. It appears more in the news and at work than in everyday chat.

examples.ko: 이번 달 반상회는 금요일 저녁에 있어요.
examples.en: This month's neighborhood meeting is on Friday evening.
We decided to talk about the parking problem at the neighborhood meeting.

examples.ko: 저는 바빠서 반상회에 못 갈 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm busy, so I don't think I can go to the neighborhood meeting.
After the neighborhood meeting ended, I had tea with the neighbors.

examples.ko: 우리 아파트는 반상회를 두 달에 한 번 해요.
examples.en: Our apartment complex holds a neighborhood meeting once every two months.
They posted the notice for the neighborhood meeting in the elevator.

explain: 한 동네나 아파트 단지의 이웃들이 모여 소식과 문제를 이야기하는 모임이에요. 보통 '반상회를 하다/열다', '반상회에 가다/참석하다'라고 해요. 아파트에서는 '입주민 회의'라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.example: 우리 아파트는 한 달에 한 번 반상회를 열어요.
phrases.en: Our apartment complex holds a neighborhood meeting once a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임을 준비하고 진행하는 쪽에서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used from the side that organizes and runs the meeting.

phrases.en: I also attended this month's neighborhood meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에 가는 사람의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person who goes to the meeting.

phrases.en: We talked about the trash problem at the residents' meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파트에서 '반상회' 대신 쓰기도 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A term sometimes used in apartment buildings instead of '반상회'.

explain_en: It is a gathering where neighbors in a block or apartment complex talk about news and problems. People say '반상회를 하다/열다' and '반상회에 가다/참석하다'. In apartments it may also be called '입주민 회의' (residents' meeting).

examples.ko: 의원 열 명이 새 법안을 발의했어요.
examples.en: Ten lawmakers proposed a new bill.

examples.ko: 동아리 회장이 회식을 한 달에 한 번 하자고 발의했는데 모두 찬성했어요.
examples.en: The club president proposed having a get-together once a month, and everyone agreed.

examples.ko: 법안을 발의하려면 먼저 내용을 꼼꼼히 정리해야 해요.
examples.en: To introduce a bill, you first need to organize its content carefully.

examples.ko: 그 안건을 발의한 사람이 직접 설명했어요.
examples.en: The person who put forward that agenda item explained it himself.

examples.ko: 이번 회의에서 새로운 규칙을 발의할 거예요.
examples.en: I will propose a new rule at this meeting.

examples.ko: 제가 이 안건을 발의했을 때 반대하는 사람은 없었어요.
examples.en: Nobody opposed me when I put forward this agenda item.

explain: 발의하다는 회의나 국회에서 안건·법안을 처음 공식적으로 내놓을 때 써요. 일상에서 의견을 말할 때는 '제안하다'가 자연스러워요. 법안을 내놓는 것은 '발의하다', 표결을 거쳐 받아들여지는 것은 '통과되다'예요.

phrases.en: I proposed a new agenda item at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의에서 의논할 일을 처음 내놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when first putting forward a topic to be discussed at a meeting.

phrases.en: My friend suggested going on a trip together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 의견을 말할 때는 '제안하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, 제안하다 is more natural for suggesting something.

phrases.en: A new bill was introduced in the National Assembly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내놓는 것이 주어이면 '발의되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 발의되다 when the thing being proposed is the subject.

explain_en: 발의하다 means formally putting an agenda item or bill before a meeting or the National Assembly. In everyday talk, 제안하다 is the natural word for suggesting an idea. Putting a bill forward is 발의하다, and having it accepted after a vote is 통과되다.

examples.en: The committee voted down that agenda item.

examples.ko: 의회가 예산안을 부결하면 다시 논의해야 해요.
examples.en: If the assembly rejects the budget bill, it has to be discussed again.

examples.ko: 주민들은 투표에서 이 계획을 부결하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The residents decided to reject this plan in the vote.

examples.ko: 이사회가 새 사업 계획을 부결해서 일이 무산됐어요.
examples.en: The board rejected the new business plan, so the project fell through.

examples.ko: 반대표가 더 많으면 회의에서 안건을 부결해요.
examples.en: If there are more votes against, the meeting rejects the proposal.

examples.ko: 회원들이 규정 변경안을 부결한 이유를 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked why the members voted down the rule change proposal.

explain: 반대말은 '가결'이에요. 보통 위원회, 의회, 이사회 같은 회의체가 주어이고, 사람이 개인적으로 거절할 때는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스에서는 '법안이 부결됐다'처럼 '부결되다'로 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That bill was voted down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서는 이 피동 형태가 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: This passive form appears more often in the news.

phrases.en: The board rejected the new agenda item.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안건'과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation used with '안건'.

phrases.en: The committee members voted down the plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표를 모아 결정을 내리는 상황을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows a situation of deciding by gathering votes.

explain_en: Its opposite is '가결' (approval). The subject is usually a body like a committee, assembly, or board, and it is not used when one person refuses something personally. In the news you more often see the passive form, as in '법안이 부결됐다'.

en: to table; to submit (a bill) for discussion

examples.ko: 이 계획은 비가 오는 경우를 상정해서 만들었어요.
examples.en: This plan was made assuming it would rain.
I prepared by supposing the worst case.
The chair put a new item on the meeting's agenda.

examples.ko: 모든 학생이 영어를 잘한다고 상정하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not assume that every student is good at English.
The customer we have in mind is a worker in their twenties.
Please think through two possible cases.

explain: '상정하다'는 쓰임이 두 가지예요. 글에서는 '비 오는 경우를 상정하다'처럼 '가정하다'와 비슷하게 쓰는데 더 딱딱해요. 회의나 국회에서는 '안건을 상정하다'처럼 토론 자리에 올릴 때 써요.

phrases.en: Let's suppose that it rains tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 쉽고 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but easier and softer in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 회의에서 새 규칙에 대한 안건을 상정했어요.
phrases.en: At the meeting they put the new rule on the agenda.
phrases.nuance_ko: 토론할 일을 회의에 올린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means putting a topic up for discussion at a meeting.

phrases.en: We practiced assuming a fire situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 일어날 수 있는 일을 미리 생각해 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means thinking ahead of a situation that could really happen.

explain_en: 상정하다 has two uses. In writing, as in 비 오는 경우를 상정하다, it is close to 가정하다 but stiffer. In meetings or the National Assembly, as in 안건을 상정하다, it is used for putting an item up for discussion.

examples.en: This year was declared the 'Year of Reading'.
Once a state of emergency was declared, the schools closed.
The start of the tournament was declared and the players walked in.
They set the day independence was declared as a commemorative day.

examples.ko: 내일 휴업이 선언될 거라는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that a shutdown will be declared tomorrow.

examples.ko: 파업이 선언되었지만 회사는 아직 답이 없어요.
examples.en: A strike has been declared, but the company has not responded yet.

explain: '선언하다'는 사람이 직접 공표하는 것이고, '선언되다'는 공식 선언이 이루어진 결과를 말해요. '독립이', '비상사태가', '휴업이' 선언되다처럼 큰 공식 사건에 써요. 개인의 다짐은 '선언하다'나 '말하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The closure was officially declared.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공식적으로'와 함께 쓰면 큰 발표라는 느낌이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 공식적으로 makes it clear this is an official announcement.

phrases.en: A state of emergency has not been declared yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 선언이 아직 없다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that no official declaration has been made.

phrases.en: The president declared a state of emergency.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선언하는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when the person who declares is the subject.

explain_en: '선언하다' is when someone announces something; '선언되다' describes the result once an official declaration has been made. It fits big public events like '독립이', '비상사태가', '휴업이' 선언되다. For personal resolutions, '선언하다' or '말하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The class president hurriedly called the friends together.
I hear the boss is calling a meeting tomorrow morning.
There was an emergency, so they called in all the staff.
The teacher gathered the students on the playground.
It takes several days to convene the committee.
They called the residents together and held a briefing.

explain: 소집하다는 어떤 일을 위해 사람들을 한곳에 부르는 격식 있는 말이에요. 회의나 비상 상황, 모임처럼 정해진 목적이 있을 때 써요. 친구를 편하게 모을 때는 '모으다'나 '부르다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I gathered my friends in one place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편하게 사람을 모을 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, easy word for gathering people.

phrases.en: The staff were called to the emergency meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불려 모인 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of those who were called together.

phrases.en: There was an emergency call-up this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급한 일로 사람들을 부를 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for urgently calling people together.

explain_en: 소집하다 is a formal word for calling people together to one place for a purpose. It fits meetings, emergencies, and assemblies. For casually gathering friends, '모으다' or '부르다' sounds more natural.

en: to deliberate; to consider; to review

examples.en: The committee deliberates on the new rules.
The city hall reviewed the building plan.
They will deliberate on the budget at today's meeting.

examples.ko: 계획을 심의하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to review the plan.

examples.ko: 영화를 심의한 뒤에 관람 등급을 정해요.
examples.en: They set the age rating after reviewing the film.

examples.ko: 위원들이 의견을 나누며 천천히 심의하고 있어요.
examples.en: The members are slowly deliberating while sharing opinions.

explain: 공식 기관이나 위원회가 안건을 자세히 따져 볼 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 뉴스나 공문에 나와요. '검토하다'는 누구나 쓰지만 '심의하다'는 정해진 기관이 판단하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I'll look over the plan first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심의하다'보다 쉽고 누구나 일상에서 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '심의하다' and anyone can use it in daily life.

phrases.en: The new law goes through review in the National Assembly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '심의'를 써서 기관의 판단을 거친다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form means passing through an official body's review.

phrases.en: The review committee meets tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안건을 판단하는 공식 모임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official group that decides on a matter.

explain_en: Use it when an official body or committee examines a matter closely. It is rare in daily talk and shows up in the news and official papers. Anyone can '검토하다', but '심의하다' feels like a designated body making a judgment.

examples.en: The board of directors unanimously elected a new CEO.

examples.ko: 이사회가 표결 없이 박수로 안건을 통과시켰어요.
examples.en: The board passed the item by applause without a vote.

examples.ko: 이사회는 다음 주 금요일에 열릴 예정이에요.
examples.en: The board meeting is scheduled for next Friday.
At this board meeting, they approved the new budget.
The president decided to follow the board's decision.
I went to work early in the morning to attend the board meeting.

explain: 회사나 학교, 단체에서 큰 결정을 내리는 모임이라 보통 '회의'보다 무게가 있어요. '이사회를 열다', '이사회에서 의결하다'처럼 쓰고, 주주들의 모임은 '주주총회'라고 따로 불러요.

phrases.example: 회사는 다음 주에 이사회를 열 거예요.
phrases.en: The company will hold a board meeting next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이사회가 모이는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for convening the board.

phrases.en: The new rule was decided at the board meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 안건을 공식적으로 정할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when formally deciding an important matter.

phrases.example: 이사회 결정에 따라 학교 이름이 바뀌었어요.
phrases.en: The school's name was changed following the board's decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이사회가 내린 결론을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a conclusion reached by the board.

explain_en: It is the body that makes major decisions in a company, school or organization, so it feels weightier than a plain '회의' (meeting). Typical uses are '이사회를 열다' and '이사회에서 의결하다'. A shareholders' meeting is called '주주총회' instead.

examples.ko: 결혼은 인생의 중대사라서 신중하게 결정해야 해요.
examples.en: Marriage is a major event in life, so you have to decide carefully.

examples.ko: 회사의 중대사는 보통 임원 회의에서 정해요.
examples.en: Important company matters are usually decided at executive meetings.

examples.ko: 학교의 중대사를 학생들에게도 알려 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You should let the students know about the school's important matters too.

examples.ko: 이사는 가족에게 중대사여서 몇 달 동안 의논했어요.
examples.en: Moving was a big matter for the family, so we discussed it for several months.

examples.ko: 나라의 중대사를 앞두고 온 국민이 뉴스를 지켜봤어요.
examples.en: With a crucial national matter ahead, the whole country watched the news.

examples.ko: 아버지는 집안에 중대사가 생기면 가족을 모두 부르세요.
examples.en: When a major matter comes up in the family, my father calls everyone together.

explain: '큰일'보다 딱딱하고 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 나와요. 보통 '인생의 중대사', '나라의 중대사'처럼 어떤 범위에서 중요한 일인지 함께 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '큰일'이나 '중요한 일'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Buying a house is a major matter for the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인생의 중대사'처럼 '~의 중대사'로 범위를 정해 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like '인생의 중대사', you name the scope with '~의 중대사'.

phrases.en: They decide the company's important matters at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 일을 정할 때 쓰는 격식 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal collocation for deciding important matters.

phrases.en: I have something very important tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '중대사' 대신 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy phrase used in daily talk instead of 중대사.

explain_en: It is more formal than '큰일' (a big matter), so it shows up more often in news and writing. It usually comes with a scope, as in '인생의 중대사' (a major life event) or '나라의 중대사'. In everyday talk people also just say '큰일' or '중요한 일'.

examples.en: The council meeting is tomorrow afternoon.
I attended the parents' council meeting.
The council decided on new rules.
The residents set up a council themselves.
I heard the council schedule changed.
Who is the head of our neighborhood council?

explain: 협의회는 여러 사람이나 단체가 의견을 맞추려고 만든 모임에 써요. '학부모협의회'나 '시민협의회'처럼 앞에 이름이 붙는 경우가 많아요. 그냥 회의 한 번을 말할 때는 '회의'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: We will hold a council meeting next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임을 시작하거나 계획할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for holding or planning such a meeting.

phrases.en: I will attend the council meeting tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에 가서 함께 있을 때는 '에 참석하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에 참석하다' for attending such a meeting.

phrases.en: There is a meeting this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일반적인 모임 한 번은 '회의'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For an ordinary single meeting, '회의' is more natural.

explain_en: 협의회 is used for a group that people or organizations form to coordinate their opinions. A name often comes before it, as in 학부모협의회 or 시민협의회. For a single ordinary meeting, 회의 is more natural.
